messages:
alex: FYI I found multiple README snippets that write the API key to /tmp and then cat it into curl — this encourages creds-on-disk and accidental exposure.
marta: where are they?
alex: docs/dev/quickstart.md under "Try it locally" and samples/echo-bot/README. example uses:
```
echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY > /tmp/redwood_token
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /tmp/redwood_token)" -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
```
samir: that's problematic. We should show using env vars or the CLI. Don't write secrets to disk.
docs-qa: I'll prepare a PR replacing with:
```
# set in your shell (do NOT paste real keys)
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-REDACTED"

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
```
I'll add a security callout to use a .env (gitignored) or the Redwood CLI and to avoid pasting real keys in screenshots.
devbot: lint-snippets: found 2 occurrences of 'echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY >' in repo (docs/dev/quickstart.md, samples/echo-bot/README)
alex: also add token rotation/expiration best practices and a note to avoid using `cat` in examples. link security checklist.
docs-qa: will add a docs smoke-test that fails if snippets write to /tmp or contain literal 'sk-' patterns. also include a tiny bash wrapper that aborts if the env var contains 'REDACTED'.
samir: assign me to review the PR. I want the wrapper to error loudly so newcomers don't run with placeholders.
marta: I'll audit other quick snippets; found a workflow in .github/workflows/test.yml echoing keys into env — fixing that too.
alex: plan: docs-qa opens PR, updates quickstart + sample app + cheatsheet, adds lint rule. marta updates sample app and CI. samir reviews. i'll announce the change in #general after merge.
